newsitem.title: GERMANY: Nervous German stocks slide in late IBIS trade.
newsitem.headline: Nervous German stocks slide in late IBIS trade.

text.p: German shares plunged in afternoon electronic trade on Wednesday after jittery markets reacted sharply to an unwelcome fall in U.S. Treasuries and surrendered ground made up over bourse trade.

Shares fell anew after a lower opening on the Dow Jones Industrial index on Wall Street and by 1347 GMT the IBIS DAX index stood at 3,220.77 points, down 60.69 points or 1.85 percent, just off a low of 3,214.48 points.
"This market is paranoid and nervous about everything and is responding dramatically to every sort of pressure. It is also a very technical market," said one equities trader.

The Dow Jones Industrial index was down over half a percent at 6,574.79 points as Frankfurt trade ended, driving German shares further down and conclusively penetrating the 3,300 point support threshold mentioned earlier by dealers.
Losses were spread pretty much across the board. The major sectors, such as the banks and the chemical companies, experienced heavy losses.
Deutsche Bank ended down 1.48 marks at 88.60 marks, while Dresdner Bank ended the day down 13 pfennigs at 44.71 marks and Commerzbank ended down 1.39 marks at 44.71 marks.
Early features, such as chemical giant BASF AG, which went higher after it gave an upbeat outlook for the current business year, was also hit by the slide.
BASF ended down 96 pfennigs at 59.69 marks. Other chemical stocks also fell at the last, including Bayer, down 1.24 marks at 66.40 marks, and Hoechst, down 1.20 marks at 63.20 marks.
